It is permissible that this be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: the great matter is indicated, while the state is that whoever ﴿exalts the rites of God﴾, that is, the markers of the religion of the Greatest King (p-45) which He urged and commanded to be performed in the Ḥajj. (The word) shaʿāʾir is the plural of shaʿīra, which means the rite and the sign in the Ḥajj. Shaʿīra also means the camel sacrificed as an offering to the Sacred House. Al-Baghawi said: its origin is from ishʿār, which is informing about it so that it is known that it is an offering (hady), and the discussion ended. Perhaps it is derived from shaʿar (hair), because when it is wounded, some of its hair is cut off or removed from the place of the wound, so it would come from removal. Exalting them means considering them good. So exalting them is better for him, because it indicates the piety of his heart. ﴿For indeed it﴾, that is, their exaltation, ﴿is from﴾, that is, beginning from, ﴿the piety of hearts﴾, which by nature perceives what is worthy of being exalted, so the one who exalts them is pious. It is known from what I have mentioned that the clause of the good has been omitted from this verse, and from His saying ﴿And whoever exalts the sacred things of God﴾ [22:30] the cause of its being good for him, which is piety. He indicated its intended meaning there by mentioning it here, and here the fact that exalting is good has been omitted, and he indicated it by mentioning it there. Thus in each clause he mentioned what indicates what was omitted from the other, as was previously discussed in ﴿There has already been for you a sign in the two groups﴾ [3:13] in Āl ʿImrān. This is called iḥtibāk (a rhetorical device in which parallel omitted elements in two clauses are mutually indicated). My interpretation of the shaʿāʾir by what I have mentioned, as a general matter, is permissible in intention, and the repetition of the pronoun referring to a type of it constitutes a type of istikhdam (a rhetorical device in which a word is used in one sense and a pronoun refers to it in another sense).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 33:

So His saying ﴿For you therein﴾ means: the camels (al-budn) or the sacrificial livestock (al-ni'am al-muhdah), or in general, ﴿benefits﴾ through milk, offspring, riding, and the like. Therefore, the fatter and finer they are, the greater their benefits become, both in religion and in worldly life. ﴿Until an appointed term﴾ is the death which We have decreed for every soul, or the slaughter if they are offered as gifts, or something other than that. This is an explanation of the sentence preceding it, for the benefits lead people of insight to reflect upon them, especially with their variation. Reflection upon them leads to piety (taqwa) through knowing that they are from Allah, that He is capable of what He wills, and that He has no partner.

And since these benefits are worldly, and the benefit of their slaughter when offered is religious, he pointed to the magnification of the second with the particle of delay, so He said: ﴿Then their place of sacrifice﴾, that is, the time at which their slaughter becomes due when you finish with them, ﴿is at the Ancient House﴾, that is, at its precincts, which is the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram), as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95].

And since the sense is: He, glory be to Him, made these things rites for you, He connected to it His saying: ﴿And for every community﴾, that is, among the earlier nations and others, ﴿We have appointed﴾ by Our majesty, which cannot be opposed, ﴿a rite (mansak)﴾, that is, a worship, or a place of worship, or a sacrifice. It is the verbal noun of nasaka (in the patterns naṣara and karuma), nusuk and mansak, and it may also mean the place in which one worships and in which the sacrificial offering (nusuk), which is the animal offering (hady), is slaughtered. Ibn Kathir said: The slaughter of sacrificial animals and the shedding of their blood in the name of God has never ceased to be prescribed in all the religious communities. (p-47)

Then He followed this appointment with its cause, as an explanation, because it is not intended in itself, and He said: ﴿that they may mention﴾. And since the religion is easy and tolerant, possessing ease, He accepted entry into it outwardly, and so He said: ﴿the name of God﴾, that is, the King, the Most High, alone, over their slaughtered animals, their offerings and all their worship, because He alone is their Provider. Then He gave the reason for the mention as being the blessing, as a reminder to reflect upon it, and so He said: ﴿over what He has provided them﴾, whereupon their thanks to Him for it becomes obligatory upon them, ﴿from the beasts of cattle﴾.

Since it is known that the Lawgiver of all true laws is one, and that the reason for His establishing them is the mention of Him alone, His saying follows from this: ﴿So your God﴾, that is, the One who prescribed all these rites. Since God (ilah) is the one who is entitled to divinity by what has been established of His attributes, and not whoever is named a god, He said: ﴿is one God﴾, and described Him with His saying: ﴿one﴾, that is, even if the branches of His laws differ and some of them abrogate others (naskh). Had He limited Himself to "one" alone, their obstinate ones might have said: the intent is our restriction to one of what we worship. He turned to address (iltifat) them directly, because that is clearer and more fitting for acceptance.

Since His being one has been established, His exclusive right to worship is necessary, and for this reason He said: ﴿so to Him﴾, that is, to Him alone, ﴿submit﴾, that is, yield with all your outward and inward being (p-48) in everything He has commanded or forbidden, whether abrogated or not, and even if you do not understand its meaning, as with most of the rites of the Hajj.

Since He commanded submission to those who need it, whether in its bringing into being, its perfection, or its continuance, and since submission is the ease of yielding without arrogance or haughtiness, and since the source of tranquility and humility, which are most fitting to the state of the pilgrims, who are stripped of stitched garments, bare-headed, seeking the removal of their burdens and the lightening of their loads, and the covering of their shame, God, glory be to Him and exalted, turned to the head of those commanded, who possesses what created beings can attain of the ranks of perfection and the qualities of beauty and majesty, as an indication that no one can reach him in that. So He said: ﴿And give good tidings to the humble﴾, that is, the lowly and the broken-hearted, from al-Khabt, meaning low-lying ground suitable for passage and other benefits.

Then He described their marks, saying: ﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned﴾ —that is, the One who possesses majesty and beauty— ﴿their hearts tremble﴾ —that is, they fear with a disquieting fear— ﴿their hearts﴾.

Since the discussion concerns the Hajj, and that is a setting that tends to bring about much mingling, which in turn tends to produce many annoyances—especially since most of those mingling were polytheists, as the sura is Meccan—He said, connecting by conjunction without a following sequence, to indicate firmness in these attributes: ﴿and the patient ones﴾, those for whom patience has become their habit, ﴿over what befalls them﴾ (p-49) whatever it may be.

Since that is a preoccupation that distracts from the prayer, He said: ﴿and those who establish the prayer﴾. That is, even if hardships befall them through the acts of the Hajj and other things, whatever may befall them, they still perform it. For this reason He expressed it by the attribute rather than the verb, indicating that none establishes it in the prescribed manner amid those hardships and preoccupations except those firmly rooted in love for it. Thus they—because of the extent to which its love is established in their hearts, and their fear of heedlessness concerning it—are as if they were always in prayer.

Since what is involved in it of increased expenditure may sometimes deter one from it, He encouraged it by saying: ﴿and from what We have provided them﴾. So, since it is a blessing from Us, they do not withhold it, and out of reverence for Our greatness they think well of the replacement ﴿they spend﴾, that is, they renew its giving continually, through gifts whose prices they exaggerate and other things, doing good to the creatures of Allah, in compliance with His command, like the low ground that gives forth what the Exalted places in it of water and pasture.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 36:

When He, glorified be He, had urged the offering of all livestock as a means of drawing near to Him, and camels were the greatest of them in creation and the most magnificent in their own estimation, He singled them out for mention in a context where they are mentioned twice, and He expressed it with the proper noun that indicates their greatness. Or [it may be that] He singled them out because He specified the Arabs with them, to the exclusion of the earlier nations. So He said, conjoining it to His words ﴿We have made it a rite (mansak)﴾ [al-Hajj: 34]. Or the reading may be, and God knows best: "We have given you a share, along with the earlier nations (p-50), in the cattle and the sheep, and ﴿the camels (al-budn)﴾, that is, the camels, namely those known for the bulk of their bodies, ﴿We have made them﴾, that is, by Our greatness. He increased the reminder of greatness by mentioning the proper name, and said: ﴿for you among the symbols (sha'a'ir) of God﴾, that is, the markers (a'lam) of the religion of the Greatest King and His rites (manasik), which He prescribed for you and in which He prescribed the ish'ar (marking), which is to pierce its hump with an iron instrument, to distinguish what is of them as an offering (hady) from other than it.

When He drew attention to the religious benefit in them, He drew attention to what is more general than that, and said: ﴿for you therein is good﴾, through subjugation, which is among the benefits of this world, and through drawing near, which is among the benefits of the Hereafter. At-Tirmidhi related it and graded it good, and Ibn Majah [related] from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The son of Adam does no deed on the Day of Sacrifice more beloved to Allah than the shedding of blood. Indeed, it will come on the Day of Resurrection with its horns, its hooves and its hair, and indeed the blood falls into a place with Allah before it falls onto the earth, so be content with it." And ad-Daraqutni in as-Sunan [related] from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Wealth was never spent on anything better than a sacrificed camel on the day of 'Id.'"

When He mentioned what is in them, He made gratitude a consequence of it, and said: ﴿So mention the name of Allah﴾, that is, the One who has no namesake, ﴿over them﴾, that is, over slaughtering them, by saying takbir, while they are (p-51) ﴿standing in rows (sawaff)﴾, standing, their left forelegs tied. Had it not been for His magnifying by obedience to His laws, He would not have prescribed for you their slaughter nor given you power over them, although they are greater than you in body and stronger. ﴿Then when their sides fall (wajabat junubuha)﴾, that is, they collapse in a fall by which they become still, their souls having departed, so that they have no movement at all. Ibn Kathir said: It has come in a marfu' hadith, "Do not hasten the soul to depart," and ath-Thawri related it in his Jami' from Ayyub, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Farafisah al-Hanafi, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said this.

Since one might think that eating from them is forbidden because of the command to bring them near to Allah, the Most High, He said, negating that: ﴿So eat from them﴾, if they are voluntary, if you wish to eat, for that does not remove them from being an offering. ﴿And feed the one who is content (al-qani') and the one who is in need (al-mu'tarr)﴾, that is, the one who presents himself to beg with humility and submission, and the one who asks; and it is said, the reverse, which is the statement of ash-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. He said in the Kitab Ikhtilaf al-Hadith: "The qani' is the beggar, and the mu'tarr is the visitor and the passer-by." Ar-Razi said in al-Lawami': The root meaning in the language is that the letters qaf, nun and 'ayn indicate turning toward a thing, then its meanings differ while the analogy remains consistent. Thus al-qani' is the beggar, because he turns toward the one he asks, and al-qani' is also the content one who does not ask, as if he is turned toward the thing with which he is content.

Since subjecting them to such slaughter in this manner, despite their strength and size, is a striking matter to the intellect upon reflection, He drew attention to it, to prompt the question about what is even greater than it, and said: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like this great subjugation ﴿We have subjected them﴾ (p-52) by Our greatness, without which that would not be ﴿for you﴾, and We made them docile night and day despite their size and strength. ﴿Had We willed, We would have made them wild﴾. ﴿That perhaps you may give thanks﴾, that is, so that you reflect on that and recognize that none has driven them to you except Allah, so that your state becomes the state of one whose gratitude is hoped for, and you render thanks by not forbidding from them except what He forbade, nor making lawful except what He made lawful, and by witnessing from them what He urged regarding their gifting, and by dealing with them according to what He commanded you.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 37:

When He urged drawing near to Him through them, with His name mentioned over them, and this was among the noble morals, and most of them used to do it, and they used to sprinkle the House and the like with the blood of their sacrifices, and cut up the meat and place it around it, claiming that this was an act of drawing near, and some of this had been an earlier law, He, glorified is He, alerted to the abrogation of that by pointing out that the intended purpose of it is its spirit, not its outward form, and so He said: ﴿It does not reach﴾, i.e., does not attain, arrive at, or perceive.

Since the context is urging drawing near to Him, glorified is He, placing His name before the doer was more fitting, for the swift negation of what may be imagined to reach Him of benefit or harm, (p-53) so He said, expressing by the proper name that guards against association in every respect: ﴿God﴾, i.e., the pleasure of the King who possesses the attributes of perfection, so no benefit or harm reaches Him. ﴿Their flesh﴾, which is eaten, ﴿nor their blood﴾, which is spilled, ﴿but what reaches Him is piety﴾, i.e., the act of the heart, which is the quality intended to shield its possessor from the wrath of God, and which has taken hold of his heart until it moves him to carry out the commands which are the ultimate ends of that, ﴿from you﴾, the motivating force for drawing near by which there is the spirit of acceptance, the attainer of what is hoped for. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': This is evidence that sincere intention is better than the prescribed acts. Its end. So when the intention reaches Him, glorified is He, before the act, then the morsel is placed [in the hand of God], "and He nurtures it as one of you nurtures his foal until it becomes like a mountain," and "the blood fell upon a place." So the negation is of a form that has no spirit, and the affirmation is of the very spirit. Intention alone may benefit without action, as the Prophet ﷺ said concerning the expedition to Tabuk, its meaning being: "There are men in Madinah whom we did not descend to a station nor cross a valley except that they were with us, held back by the excuse." Action without intention does not benefit, and it is intention that brings the reward everlastingly. And God is the Granter of success. Then He repeated the reminder of the great subjection of these [animals], alerting them to what He obligated upon them by it, and so He said: ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., this great subjection, ﴿He subjected them﴾, i.e., God, who combines the attributes of perfection, ﴿to you﴾, by His greatness and His independence from you, ﴿that you may magnify﴾

When He mentioned magnifying, He expressed it with the greatest Name, so He said: ﴿God﴾. Magnifying was made to include the act of thanking, so the implied meaning is: thanking Him ﴿for guiding you﴾ (p-54), i.e., for His guidance of you to it and to the great matters to which He guided you.

Since religion does not stand except by warning and good tidings, and the context concerns the rites of Hajj and the landmarks of raising the voice in talbiyah and shedding blood, good tidings were more fitting. He mentioned it, alluding to the warning by the conjunction "and," to indicate that the implied meaning is: "So warn, O caller, the evildoers," and then: ﴿And give good tidings to the doers of good﴾, i.e., those who have brought goodness into their deeds, in form and in meaning.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 38:

When He, glorified be He, mentioned the Hajj, which reminds the emigrants (al-muhajirin) of their homelands from which they were expelled, and the dispute (al-mukhasamah) that was revealed concerning the battle of Badr, and mentioned the acts of worship (al-qurubat) performed in it, the longing of souls for that grew intense. They recalled the overbearing of the polytheists (al-mushrikin), who bar from the way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque, and their dominance, and their prevention of those who wished to perform these acts, in these pure attributes and good states, and their persecution of them. So He answered this question, glorified be He, with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One for whom there is no equal, ﴿defends those who believe﴾. For, by entering into faith, they had not been excessive in treachery or in disbelief, so He loves them. How much more so, then, the good-doers, with whom the preceding verse was concluded. That is, He will give them victory over their enemy. This is in the recitation of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub without an alif, and in the recitation of the rest, with an alif, as an intensification, by expressing the verb in the sense of contest (al-mughalabah). It is as if He had said: Give them the good news that Allah defends them. However, He, exalted be He, made the attributes apparent so that it is understood that they are the basis (manat) of the rulings and of the expression. So He expressed it with the past tense to encourage, that is, for everyone who actualized this attribute in external reality, actualizing it to any degree, He would defend him. Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿does not love﴾, that is, does not honor as the lover does, ﴿every treacherous﴾ in his trust, preventing His servants from His house which is for people equally, the one dwelling in it and the outsider, ﴿ungrateful﴾ for His blessing by seeking nearness to other than Him. Such a person performs noble morals in form only, in which there is no meaning at all; it is not made sound by mentioning Allah alone, nor beautified by good-doing. He brought the two attributes in the intensive form (sighat al-mubalaghah) because the deficiencies of a human cannot be performed devoid of intensification, for he betrays himself first by resolve, second by the act, and third by other creatures; likewise he betrays himself and his Lord, glorified be He, and so in disbelief and otherwise. And since treachery is the source (manba') of deficiencies, intensification in it is greater.

(p-56) Since it was as if it had been asked, "How will the repelling take place, and by whom?", it was said: "By His believing servants." He expressed this by His saying ﴿Permission is given﴾. By the reading of the one who vocalized it in the passive form (*majhul*, the unnamed-agent voice), he indicated the ease of this matter for Him, glory be to Him. ﴿To those who are fought against﴾, meaning, to those who have the strength to repel, by means of fighting, after they had been restrained from it in Makkah and commanded to forbear. Then he mentioned the cause of the permission and said ﴿because they have been wronged﴾, meaning, the injustice of the wrongdoers befell them through expulsion from their homes and harm without right.

Since the implied sense was, "Indeed Allah willed to make His religion prevail through them," he joined to it His saying ﴿And indeed Allah﴾, meaning, the One who is the Supreme King, in whose grip is everything. It is also permissible for it to be joined to His saying ﴿Indeed Allah defends﴾ [al-Hajj: 38], meaning, with His permission for them to fight, and that He ﴿is able to give them victory﴾. This is more emphatic in affirmation, because the victory was considered unlikely at that time given the disbelievers' numbers and strength, and the believers' weakness and scarcity. So He said: ﴿is certainly All-Powerful﴾.

Then He described them with that which makes clear their state of being wronged, in a manner that unites them and makes them trust in God, so He said: ﴿Those who have been driven from their homes﴾ to al-Shi'b, Abyssinia, and Madina, ﴿without right﴾, which required that, ﴿except that they say﴾, that is, other than their saying, or ﴿except their saying﴾: ﴿Our Lord is God﴾, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, the One who necessitates their remaining in their homes, their being loved and praised, and their following of His traces. So it is of the type of the verse:

*"There is no fault in them, except that their swords, by them, are notched from the clashing of the battalions."*

In arranging the statement in this manner, the exception, according to those who take it as disjunctive (munqati'), is an indication that whoever is sincere to God, people aim at him the arrows of their deceit, and they leave nothing of their effort in harming him.

When He mentioned His repelling (of harm) and mentioned that it was for the believers, He explained its secret in general terms so that this specific case could be understood from it, and He depicted it to bring it closer to understanding. So He said, conjoining it to what its estimation implies: Had it not been for God's permission to them, shirk would have continued openly, and falsehood, through the domination of the ignorant over the places of pilgrimage, would have prevailed. ﴿And had it not been for God's repelling﴾, that is, the One encompassing everything in knowledge and power, in every sacred law and in the time of every prophet He sent, ﴿the people﴾, that is, in general, ﴿some of them by means of others﴾, that is, by giving some of them power over others, ﴿monasteries would have been demolished﴾, and they are small, elevated places of worship for monks, ﴿and churches﴾ for the Christians, ﴿and synagogues﴾, that is, the churches of the Jews, ﴿and mosques﴾, that is, for the Muslims. He placed it last so that it would be far from demolition and near to remembrance, ﴿in which the name of God is mentioned much﴾, that is, the King to whom there is no king other than Him. Perhaps the shift from the pronoun to the explicit noun is to indicate the difference, which He mentioned, among the places mentioned, in sincerity and otherwise. ﴿Much﴾, because every sect wants to demolish what belongs to the other, and indeed one of the people of a religion may wish to ruin some of the places of worship of his own religion; yet God repels it through whomever He wills of His servants. If you reflect on this, you will find in it secrets that are too subtle for thoughts, for when God intended the corruption of most people, He set up for them of opposites what greatly lightens their obstinacy.

Since the estimation was: "But the mentioned places were not demolished, because God repelled some of them by means of others and placed some of them against the throats of others," He conjoined to it, or to His saying ﴿permission has been given﴾ [al-Hajj: 39], His saying: ﴿God will surely help﴾, that is, the Greatest King, and He used the explicit noun rather than the pronoun to generalize and to attach the ruling to the attribute: ﴿whoever helps Him﴾, whoever he may be among them or others, through what He prepares for him of means, proceeding with him in the customary way, or without means, breaking the habit, as occurred in many conquests, such as al-'Ala' ibn al-Hadrami (may God be pleased with him) crossing the salt sea to Jawathan in Bahrain, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may God be pleased with him) plunging into the Tigris, despite its greatness in that year, its flood, its rising and its height, and the shaking of the walls of Homs by takbir and the collapse of many of its houses despite the perfection of their construction and the firmness of their foundations and pillars, and similar things. Then He gave the reason for His help, even though the one helped may be weak, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is All-Powerful, All-Mighty﴾, that is, the One to whom none is equal, ﴿strong﴾ in what He wills, ﴿mighty﴾, such that no one can overpower Him. Whoever has Him as helper is the victorious, and his enemy is the vanquished. Indeed, He, glory be to Him, has spoken truly in what He promised, so He humbled, through the helpers of His religion (may God be pleased with them), the tyrants and kings of the earth, and who is more truthful in speech than God?

When He described Himself, glory be to Him, with what necessitates the empowering of His helper who supports him, He described them with what shows that their fighting is for Him, not for themselves, after He had described them as having been harmed by expulsion from their homes, which is equivalent to killing. So He said: ﴿Those who﴾. Since the time of victory was undetermined, its end being the Day of Decision, He used the particle of doubt so that this would more clearly show the sincerity of the sincere in fighting: ﴿if We establish them﴾ by Our greatness ﴿in the land﴾ by raising them above their opponents, ﴿they establish the prayer﴾, that is, the one which is the pillar (ʿimad) of the religion and which indicates watchfulness and turning away from seeking what is perishable; ﴿and give the zakah﴾, which signals renunciation of what is acquired from it and signals the soul's preparation for departure; ﴿and enjoin what is right﴾, which is what the Law has made known and permitted; ﴿and forbid what is wrong﴾, which is known to be that for which they have no comfort except in Him, glory be to Him, no fear except of Him, and no hope except in Him. The verse indicates the validity of the caliphate (khilafa) of the four Imams.

Since this was the beginning of the command to jihad, and it came after his enemies had harmed his allies, and their harm to them had lasted long, the implied meaning, as indicated by the conjunction with something not mentioned, is as follows. It is conjoined to ﴿And were it not for the repelling﴾ [al-Hajj: 40]. ﴿So to Allah belongs the beginning of affairs﴾; He conjoined to it His words: ﴿And to Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King who encompasses everything, ﴿belongs the outcome of affairs﴾. So their empowerment is certain to occur, but mentioning it as the outcome and omitting it as the beginning alerts that He, exalted is He, gives Satan, as is mostly observed, a portion in the beginning, so that the truthful may be distinguished from the liar and the wavering from the steadfast. As for the outcome, it is purely His until the Last Day, when no one will have any command, and no one will speak except by specific permission. Since these verses contain both encouragement and warning that move the intelligent and crush the ignorant, the ruling for the intelligent was omitted because what preceded makes it understood, namely: ﴿If they believe in you, We will establish them in the land﴾. This was indicated by conjoining the ruling for the ignorant to something not mentioned, in a context that consoles His Prophet ﷺ, comforts him, gives him companionship and sympathy. So He said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 42:

﴿And if they deny you﴾, that is, I seized them, even though they were the most powerful of people. And We did that to those before them, so do not let their affair grieve you. ﴿Then the people of Noah denied (their messengers)﴾ — and He, glorified is He, used the feminine ta' (تاء التأنيث) to belittle those who denied His power, even though they were the strongest of people.

Since these nations were great in stature and their times were long, as if they had filled all of time, He did not use the preposition (الجار, al-jar) and said: ﴿before them, the people of Noah﴾. They were (p-٦١) the longest-lived of people and the most powerful in capability. Since no purpose in this context depended on varying their order, He arranged them according to their order of existence, saying: ﴿and ʿĀd﴾, that is, those of strong bodies, ﴿and Thamūd﴾, those of tall buildings, in the plains and the mountains.

Translation:

﴿And the people of Abraham﴾: the tyrants, the arrogant. ﴿And the people of Lot﴾: the defiled, through that which none of mankind had committed before them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 44:

﴿And the people of Madyan﴾: the lords of wealth, gathered from the treasuries of misguidance.

Since Musa (peace be upon him) had brought signs, first visible and then audible, the like of which no one before him had brought, his being denied was extremely far-fetched. So Allah, glorified is He, changed the style as a reminder of this, and to indicate that those who unanimously denied him were the Copts, whereas among his own people only a few denied him. So He said: ﴿And Musa was denied﴾. In this there is also a magnification of consolation for the one being consoled, and an exaltation of solace. ﴿Then I gave the disbelievers respite﴾, meaning: then, following their denial, I granted them respite by postponing their punishment until the appointed time I had set for them. He expressed the length of the respite with the particle of delay (thumma) to increase the consolation, so He said: ﴿Then I seized them﴾. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, drew attention to the fact that in their seizure there were lessons and wonders, and terrors and marvels, through the interrogative in His words: ﴿Then how was My disapproval?﴾, meaning: how was My rejection of their deeds. So let these people, to whom you have brought the greatest thing any messenger brought to his people, take heed of the like of that.

(p-٦२) Since these seven nations were the majority of the people of the earth, indeed one nation of them was "the people of the earth," as its explanation has passed in Surat al-A'raf, how much more so for those other than them, from among those who lived in their times and after them. Allah, glorified and exalted, informed that His custom with them was respite followed by destruction. From this there arose an emphasis in reporting them and in their large number. So He, exalted, said, explaining the seizing and the granting of respite in the manner of the "scrambled arrangement" (al-nashr al-mushawwash, a rhetorical style in which the elements are mentioned out of their order): ﴿How many a town have We destroyed﴾, like these mentioned ones and others. In the recitation of the community, other than Abu 'Amr, with the nun (we), it is an expression of magnificence (the "recitation" being a mode of reciting the Qur'an). ﴿And it was wrongdoing﴾, that is, while the situation was that it was ﴿wrongdoing, so it was﴾, that is, so there resulted from its destruction that it was ﴿fallen down upon its roofs﴾, that is, collapsed and in ruins, meaning its walls ﴿upon its roofs﴾, that is, its ceilings, in that the wooden beams broke apart, and not from the abundance of rains or other secrets, so they fell, and then the walls fell upon them. Or the meaning is: empty, its souls having departed with the departure of its inhabitants, while its ceilings remain, needing nothing but its inhabitants. (And) how many a "deserted well" has been left without its people, while its structure remains and its water gushes forth. ﴿And a lofty palace﴾, that is, high, well-built, plastered, for only that which is intended to be raised is built up (shuyyida, meaning plastered). So the palaces were stripped of their owners, and became desolate and forlorn, empty of all their companions, after the great crowding of their gathering places, and the wells were left without their drawers of water, after the throng between those who came in the morning and those who went out in the evening, near and far, settled and nomadic. Since the ruin of what is built up weakens its pillars and wears away its walls, the emphatic form (tashdid) was not appropriate in describing the palace, as it was appropriate in describing the well.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 46:

When this was an admonition to whoever has insight, and an inducement to the Mighty, the Forgiving, the denunciation of them for their failure to take heed followed from it. He counted their journeys, in which they saw these towns in the manner that He, glory be to Him, had described, as non-existent, since they were in that manner. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land?﴾ That is, while they were possessed of sight, looking with their eyes at what they passed by, of the visible signs in the wrongdoing, destroyed towns and others. The incitement to travel indicates sight.

Since the answer is in the subjunctive (naṣb), it is known that it is negated, because it is a consequence of the interrogative hamza of denunciation, whose meaning is negation. It has entered upon the negation of travel and so negated it, thereby affirming travel, free of what the answer conveys, which is His saying ﴿so that they would have﴾, that is, so that there would result from their travelling that they would have ﴿hearts﴾ attentive ﴿with which they understand﴾ what they saw with their eyes of the visible signs of the evidence of God, exalted is He, for His oneness and His power to give life and cause death whenever He wills, so that they would take heed by it. Thus the non-existence of the described hearts depends on the negation of travel, which is the affirmation of travel. The same applies to the ears in His saying ( or ), that is, or they would have, if they were blind of sight, (p-64) as is indicated by making this a counterpart: ﴿ears with which they hear﴾ the audible signs conveyed from those towns and others, whether they travelled or not, if their insight was not penetrating in understanding by mere sight, so that they would reflect upon them with their hearts. For the loss of sight does not harm them when insight is present.

Since what harms a person is only the blindness of insight and not of sight, He negated blindness of sight altogether, since there is no necessity of harm with the illumination of insight. He restricted it to sight because harm exists in it, and even if sight existed, it would be a consequence of what has passed, along with what it indicates of the estimation. So He said: ﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that are blinded﴾, that is, because there is no harm in their blindness for one whose insight is illuminated, ﴿but it is the hearts that are blinded﴾ which are in the breasts. He emphasised the meaning with His saying ﴿which are in the breasts﴾, because harm exists in their blindness, which nullifies the benefit of their possessor even if sight is present. So in depicting their blindness there was need for additional specification, since it is customarily understood that blindness pertains only to sight, to inform that the hearts were not mentioned by mistake but deliberately, as an alert that blindness of sight is a non-entity in comparison with their blindness. By "the heart" is meant a subtle divine, spiritual essence deposited in the conical flesh deposited on the left side of the chest, to which there is an attachment... The intellects of most people hold that it resembles the attachment of an accident to a body, or of an attribute to what it qualifies, or of one who is located to a place. (p-65) This subtle essence is, in the reality of the human being, called "heart" by way of proximity and attachment. It is like the rider, while the whole body is like the horse. The blindness of the rider is more harmful to the rider than the blindness of the horse. Indeed, there is no comparison at all between the two harms in the ultimate sense. Therefore He negated blindness of sight altogether and absolutely. (p-66) So nothing's harm is comparable to the blindness of insight.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 47:

When He, glory be to Him, had mentioned that the one who is astray and leads others astray will suffer disgrace in this world, and had mentioned that He repels [harm] from those who believe and gives them victory, and had offered the evidence of observation for this from the ruined unjust towns whose destruction He accomplished, and concluded by denouncing their blindness to the plain signs, He said, linking it to ﴿And among people is one who argues﴾ [al-Hajj: 8], expressing wonder at them and clarifying their blindness: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾. It is also permissible, and it is the better reading, that this sentence be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to the subject of ﴿travel﴾ [al-Hajj: 46], so that it is among what He disapproved of them: ﴿the punishment﴾ with which you threaten them, in denial and mockery. (And) the circumstance is that "Allah will not fail" — the One for whom there is no equal — ﴿His promise﴾, so it must come to pass. But a long time in their reckoning is short in His reckoning. He may fulfil the promise, or He may delay it after the threat, to a period of a day or less or more, because His decree has preceded that it will occur only at its appointed time, for wisdoms that He reveals to whomever of His servants He wills. ﴿And indeed a day﴾, that is, one day, ﴿with your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to you by delaying (p-67) the punishment from them as an honour to you, ﴿is like a thousand years﴾. Since the intended meaning here is length of time, He expressed it with "year" to draw attention to this. And since years may vary, He said: ﴿of what you count﴾, because your days suit your imaginations and your times suit your circumstances. And He is Forbearing, who does not feel time to be long, and Powerful, who does not fear escape.

When He had shown the victory of His allies and the subjugation of His enemies through the testimony of those towns, and concluded with a marvelling at their hastening (for His punishment) even though they had witnessed the destruction of their likes, and had informed them of His forbearance (al-Ana'ah), the vastness of His majesty, and the greatness of His measure, He linked to ﴿fa-ka'ayyin﴾ [al-Hajj: 45] a warning against His retribution after His long respite, with His saying: ﴿And how many a town﴾, that is, of its people, ﴿I gave respite to it﴾, that is, I granted it time, as I have granted you time, ﴿while it was a wrongdoer﴾ [al-Hajj: 45], like your wrongdoing by hastening and otherwise. ﴿Then I seized it﴾, that is, with punishment, ﴿and to Me is the final return﴾, with the cutting off of every judgment other than My judgment, just as the beginning was from Me. No one can prevent the creation of what I willed to create, nor can anything be created that I did not will to create. So do not be deceived by the respite, even if the days and nights extend, and beware the consequences of ruin, even if you attain what you desire of hopes.

Perhaps He omitted mention of the beginning (al-Bad') because He is veiled in it by means (al-Asbab), so His name al-Batin (the Hidden) prevails in it. For this reason, most of creation has gone astray in this abode, by standing still with the means.

Since urging for deeds (al-isti'jal bi'l-af'al) is not sought from the Messenger, and since the report of their mockery and the severity of their blindness might perhaps convey permission to turn away from them altogether and entirely, He, glorified and exalted, said, removing that notion and alerting that the like of this is sought only from one who is sent (al-mursal), not from the Messenger (al-rasul):

﴿Say﴾, i.e., to them, and let not what We have informed you of concerning their blindness keep you from calling them: ﴿O mankind﴾, i.e., all of them, from my people and others, ﴿I am only a warner to you﴾, i.e., and a bringer of glad tidings. He omitted the latter because the context is one of warning, and security for the one who reaches its end necessarily follows from it, so the glad tidings come [by implication]. Also, warning is the greatest intended aim of the call, for none undertakes it except those strengthened with a spirit from God. ﴿Clear﴾, i.e., concerning everything that benefits you so that you adhere to it, and harms you so that you abandon it, [but] I am not a god who hastens the punishment for you.

Then, as a consequence of its being an explanation, the knowledge follows that the attribute of good tidings is intended even though it is omitted. So He, glorified is He, pointed to it by His saying, as an honouring of the people of good tidings and warning: ﴿So those who believed﴾, meaning they affirmed belief with their tongues, ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning as a confirmation of their claim to that, ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾ for whatever shortcoming had preceded from them, because no one can measure God with His true measure.

And since this was the first permission to fight (qital), which necessitates confronting the disbelievers and emigrating (hijrah) from family, wealth and homeland, and since that, despite being in the utmost severity, usually entails poverty, He said, confirming it and alerting that it is the cause of provision: ﴿and provision﴾, meaning in this world through spoils and other things, and in the Hereafter through what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human being, ﴿noble﴾, with no baseness in it, no meanness, no cessation, nor anything else at all, as long as they remain characterized by that. This is their Lord's action toward them, the reverse of what is said of the one whom the disbelievers call upon, that his harm is closer than his benefit.

When the verse is in the context of warning, he (God) expressed it in the past tense to add to the intimidation: ﴿Those who strove﴾, meaning those who engaged in striving, even once, with some doubt or the like, ﴿against Our signs﴾, meaning those which We set up as evidence of Us, whether seen or heard, ﴿seeking to frustrate [them]﴾, meaning exaggerating in doing what, in their assumption, would imply Our incapacity. It is also read *mu'ajjizin* (causing to be incapable), meaning presuming that they can render Us incapable by concealing Our signs, misguiding people and turning them away from them by casting doubts and disputation, following the rebellious Satan, without knowledge, guidance or a illuminating Book. Such is the case with the doubts of the Ittihadiyya (the Unitarian monists, adherents of the doctrine of the unity of existence), whose affair has spread among many people, although nothing is weaker than their doubts or more evidently false. For this reason their affair has spread among the foolish. The propagandist among them tells the one he deceives: "The apparent meaning of this speech is not held by any rational person; rather, what is meant by it is subtle secrets beyond the reach of the intellect, which are attained only through spiritual discipline and unveiling." The deceived one does not realise that Abu Talib was more intelligent than this man to whom that manifest disbelief is attributed. His poetry was better than his poetry, his extemporaneous speech greater than his, and his judgement sounder than his, and he witnessed from the signs of the Prophet ﷺ what has no further addition, despite his well-known kinship and his love (for him) which exceeds counting. Yet despite all that, he persisted in misguidance to a degree that a donkey would not accept, had it been able to speak. Moreover, this deceived man, by thinking well of these disbelievers, has necessarily come to think ill of the noblest of creation, the Prophet ﷺ, in his saying: "Whoever among you sees an evil..." — the hadith whose version says: "And there is nothing beyond that, i.e., disapproval in the heart, [even] the weight of a mustard seed of faith." I have written books explaining their misguidance, because of the spread of their evil and the harm they have caused, some long and some short, with no addition to their clarification and the manifestation of their authority. ﴿Those﴾, the distant and detested ones, ﴿are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, meaning deserving it because of what they strove for. If He wills, He will accept their repentance, and if He wills, He will cast them into it, so that they may know that they are the ones who are incapable. This is in the Hereafter. And in this world too, Glorified is He, He will make their incapacity manifest, by exposing their doubts and by the pure hearts rejecting them, together with their humiliation, their brokenness, their abasement and their disgrace, until they cannot utter a single word about it, knowing that a rational person would never say the like of it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 52:

When it became clear from this that Satan casts doubts into the minds of the disbelievers, by which they confound (the truth) through their disputation concerning the religion of Allah, which He commanded His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to make manifest and establish and make known, He joined to it, as consolation for him (ﷺ), His saying: ﴿And We did not send﴾, that is, by Our greatness, ﴿before you﴾. Then He emphasized the comprehensiveness with His saying: ﴿any messenger﴾, that is, any king or human being bringing a new law to which he calls, ﴿nor any prophet﴾, whether he was a messenger or not, one who is charged with preserving a previous law. This is what al-Baydawi and others said regarding the messenger, but it is refuted by the prophets of the Children of Israel who came between Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them, for Allah the Exalted called them messengers in more than one verse, such as: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book and followed him up with messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87]. Therefore the correct formulation is: the prophet (nabi) is a person to whom revelation is given of a new law or of a confirmed (existing) law; if he is commanded to convey it, then he is also a messenger. The restriction "of a law" serves to exclude Maryam and others among the saints. ﴿Except when he recites﴾, that is, recites to the people what Allah commanded him, or speaks to them about it, and desires in his soul that they accept it, out of eagerness for their faith and compassion for them, ﴿Satan casts into his recitation﴾, that is, into what he recited or spoke about and desired that they accept, from doubts and imaginings, which his allies seize from him and then dispute with them, the people of obedience, in order to lead them astray.

﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾ [al-An'am: 121]. ﴿And thus did We make for every prophet an enemy: devils among mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with decorated speech as deception﴾ [al-An'am: 112]. Just as these people do in what they alter in the face of the Shari'ah, in its fundamentals and its branches, from their saying that the Qur'an is poetry, sorcery and soothsaying; and their saying ﴿If Allah had willed, we would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 148]; and their saying ﴿These are our intercessors with Allah﴾ [Yunus: 18]; and their saying that what Allah kills by natural death is more deserving of being eaten than what is slaughtered; and their saying: "We are the people of Allah and the residents of His sanctuary; we do not leave the Haram, so we stand at the Sacred Monument during the Hajj while the people stand at 'Arafah; and we perform the circumambulation in our clothes, and likewise whoever we give birth to; but as for others, they may not circumambulate except naked, male or female, unless one of us gives him something to wear," and similar things by which they wish to extinguish the light of Allah. Likewise are the interpretations of the Batiniyyah and the Ittihadiyyah and their speculations in which they have deviated, by which Allah leads astray whom He wills, then erases them for whom He wills of His servants and of His command. ﴿Then Allah abrogates﴾, that is, as a consequence of its being cast, Allah abrogates, ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing everything in power and knowledge, ﴿what Satan casts﴾, so He nullifies it by making His matter clear and by rejecting it from hearts.

Since His nullification of the doubts, glorified is He, was a firm nullification, admitting no approach of doubt at all because of the lofty rank of His clarification, He expressed it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then Allah makes His verses firm﴾, that is, the King who has no equal makes them clear in what is intended by them. The most evident proof that this is what is meant, together with the opening with confronting (the disbelievers) in the verses, is the closing with His saying, as a conjunction with what is implied, meaning: so Allah is Powerful over whatever He wills:

﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾, that is, of the negation of doubts, ﴿Wise﴾, in presenting speech in a manner that has no effect on it for whoever has even a little insight. Likewise is what has passed in the surah and what comes later concerning disputation.

He, glorified is He, after mentioning what He had decreed regarding granting Satan power over this casting, mentioned the reason for that, saying: ﴿So that He may make what Satan casts a trial﴾, that is, in what is recited or what is spoken of, of those doubts, into the hearts of His allies, ﴿a trial﴾, that is, a test and an examination, ﴿for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, because their hearts have sunk from the limit of moderation in religion, until their watery nature accepts every form and no form remains fixed in them. They are the people of hypocrisy, who eagerly receive the doubts and cast them. ﴿And for those whose hearts are hardened﴾ against understanding the verses. They are those whose hearts have risen above that disputation until they became stony, and they are the ones who openly declare enmity. They are in doubt about their affair and dispute with the believers, and the doubts have been engraved upon them, so they have become the furthest thing from removal. Since the implied sense was: "Indeed, they are the party of Satan and the enemies of the Merciful," He followed it with His saying, "And indeed" (wa-innahum), which is originally "and indeed they are thus," but He made it manifest as an alert to their description, and He said: ﴿And indeed the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those who place their statements and actions in other than their proper places, like the one who is in darkness, ﴿are in extreme dissension﴾, that is, in opposition, by being on a side other than the side of the Party of God, by their failure to refute the verses with those doubts they received from Satan, and by disputing with them against the allies of the Merciful, ﴿far﴾ from the right course. ﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing﴾ [al-An'am: 113].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 54:

﴿And that those who have been given knowledge⁠﴾ [will know] through the perfecting of His proofs, the firmness of His demonstrations, and the weakness of the doubts of those who strive against Him (the verb has been put in the passive form to magnify its fruit in itself, not in relation to a specific giver), ﴿that it﴾, i.e., the thing you recited or related, ﴿is the truth﴾, i.e., the established reality that cannot be removed, ﴿from your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who bestows favour upon you by teaching you it. For the truth, whenever its people are disputed with, its proofs become manifest, its faces become bright, its demonstrations become clear, and its depths overwhelm, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He leads many astray by it, and He guides many by it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 26]. ﴿So that they believe in it﴾, because of what became apparent to them of its soundness through what became apparent of the weakness of those doubts, ﴿and their hearts humble themselves to Him﴾, i.e., become tranquil and submit, and their hearts become settled by it. For Allah placed tranquility in them, making them glassy, firm, pure and fine, between the watery and the stony, beneficial for understanding and memorizing knowledge and being guided by it for whoever accepts it from them among those who are astray, just as the earth benefits by the acceptance of a portion of it of a portion of the water, and the growth of what Allah decrees of herbage and other things, and the preservation of another portion for another portion of it for the drinking of animals. ﴿And indeed Allah﴾, with His majesty and greatness, is their guide, but He made clear the cause of knowledge by saying: ﴿guides those who believe⁠﴾ in (p-74) all that the friends of Satan cast, ﴿to a straight path⁠﴾ through which they reach knowledge of its falsehood, and that leads them to the happiness of both abodes.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 55:

﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease﴾ meaning: disbelief has come into existence among them, and they have been sealed upon it. ﴿in doubt﴾ meaning: in suspicion, seeking to settle into it. ﴿concerning it﴾ meaning: on account of the casting of Satan and what he cast; or it is a *mubtada'* (a subject, in the grammatical sense of the inchoative) ﴿concerning it﴾. ﴿until the Hour comes upon them﴾ meaning: death or the Resurrection, ﴿suddenly﴾ meaning: unexpectedly, through their dying a natural death (*hatf al-anf*, literally "death by the nose," i.e., dying without violence). ﴿or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day﴾ on which all their sons will be killed among them, and they will have none of what they hope for, whether victory or anything else, just as they strove with their disputation and the casting of misguidance into the nullification of the verses. So when the covering is removed from them by the Hour, or by the punishment that brings them to the point of the *ghargharah* (the death rattle), they will believe, like the beasts that perceive only particulars, but that will not benefit them, because its condition has lapsed. By the praise of Allah, this verse has been cleared of [the doubts] established by suspicions, the imaginings of resemblances have been exposed, and the misleading trials have been suppressed, namely the story of the *Gharaniq* (the "cranes") and what resembles it, which that exalted presence and that great and inviolable sanctuary are too high for. None of that is authentic, as stated clearly by the hafiz *Imad al-Din* Ibn Kathir and others. How could it be, when [Allah] has prevented Satan from taking the likeness of him ﷺ in a dream? (p-75) As he ﷺ said, related by al-Shaykhan (Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him: "Whoever sees me in a dream has indeed seen me, for Satan cannot take my form." And Allah, glorified is He, has taken upon Himself the preservation of the Wise Reminder by guarding the heavens and other things: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]. ﴿Except one whom He has approved of among messengers, for indeed He sends before him and behind him guards﴾ [al-Jinn: 27]. ﴿That He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ [al-Jinn: 28].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 56:

Since they were in such great number and strength, it was as if it were said: "How could they be defeated?" So He answered this by saying: ﴿The dominion that Day belongs to Allah﴾, that is, on the day when that [reckoning or defeat] comes to them, whether in the Hereafter or in this world, ﴿to Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection. He is singled out by the predominance of His apparent name, in that His command runs in it by means other than the causes you know.

Since it was as if it were said: "What is the meaning of its being exclusively His, when all days are His?" It was said: ﴿He will judge between them﴾, that is, between the believers and the disbelievers, by the decisive matter, with no judgment in it, outwardly or inwardly, belonging to anyone else, as you see it now. Rather, the affair proceeds in it according to the most perfect laws of justice. For this reason, the manifestation of justice from Him caused Him to state the details that follow: to make manifest His sole right to judgment, by honoring those whom they had been certain would be humiliated in both abodes (p-76), although placing them first is more suited to the aim of the surah: ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, that is, and who made true their claim of faith by doing ﴿righteous deeds﴾, which are what Allah commanded them to do.

Since His, exalted is He, reward for the people of His obedience is an act of His bounty, He drew attention to this by leaving the report unconnected to the causal fa’ (فَ, "so"), unlike what comes regarding the disbelievers. So He said: ﴿in Gardens of Bliss﴾. In this world it is figurative, because of their eventual destination toward them, together with the delight they find in intimate conversation with Allah and their sense of nearness; and in the Hereafter it is literal, by what Allah has shown them mercy with, namely His granting them success in righteous deeds.

"Those who disbelieve" (wa-alladhina kafaru), i.e., they covered over the knowledge We had given them of the proofs of Our oneness, "and denied Our signs" (wa-kadhdhabu bi-ayatina), striving, by means of the understanding We had given them, to render them powerless through disputation, with the doubts that their allies among the devils inspire in them. He joined the predicate to the subject with the fa' (fa-ulaika) to signify that it is a consequence of their disbelief, so He said: "Those" (fa-ulaika), i.e., the ones far removed from the causes of nobility, "for them is a humiliating punishment" (lahum 'adhabun muhin), because of what they strove at in demeaning Our signs, desiring to exalt themselves by overcoming them and by being arrogant toward following them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 58:

Since the polytheists were using these doubts and others like them to keep many people from faith, and they could only make these doubts take hold on those who mixed with them, He (glory be to Him) encouraged emigration (hijrah), saying: ﴿And those who emigrated﴾, i.e., who carried out the emigration from their homelands and their families, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, i.e., the path of the Possessor of Majesty and Honor which He legislated, so that it was a container (ẓarf) for their emigration, and they had no other aim in it. Since the thing most feared from emigration is being killed, through the enemies' intent to confront the emigrant in battle once hostility is established, He said, using the particle of delay (thumma) to indicate the length of life and the elevation of rank that come from emigration: ﴿then they were killed﴾, i.e., after the emigration, and He attached to this the general case of death out of His bounty, saying: ﴿or died﴾, i.e., without being killed, ﴿Allah will surely provide for them﴾, i.e., the King, the Most High, ﴿with a goodly provision﴾, from the moment their souls part from their bodies, because they are alive with their Lord. This is because they pleased Allah by what they stripped themselves of, of what they had built up over the length of their lives, and which their forefathers had built up before them: their wealth, their families, and their homes.

Since the implied sense is: indeed Allah is the doer of whatever He wills, of giving them life and provision and other things, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And indeed Allah﴾, i.e., the One who combines the attributes of perfection in His greatness and His power to give life just as He has power to cause death, ﴿is surely the best of providers﴾. He provides for creatures in general, the righteous among them and the wicked, so how about those who emigrate to Him! And He gives a gift that no counting can encompass and no limit can contain. Just as the verse indicates that whoever dies in the way of Allah while on garrison duty (ribāṭ) or otherwise is equal to the martyr in provision, so too the Sunnah indicates, from the hadith of Salman and others, may Allah be pleased with them, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies while on garrison duty, his provision continues for him and he is safe from the two testers (al-fattānayn)."

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 59:

Since provision (rizq) is not complete except with a good abode, and that is among the best of provisions, He said, indicating the conclusion of the preceding verse: ﴿He will surely admit them to an admission﴾, that is, an entrance and a place of entrance — the reading of Nafi' and Abu Ja'far with a fatha on the mim — and an admission and a place of admission according to the reading of the rest [of the readers]. ﴿with which they will be pleased﴾: they will not seek any substitute for it, because of what He has pleased them with, namely what they came out of [for His sake].

Since the implied sense is: "Indeed Allah is surely Most Appreciative (shakur), Most Praiseworthy (hamid)," and it is certain that no one can measure Allah with His due measure however hard he strives, because man is a place of error and forgetfulness, and were he to be held accountable for that he would perish, and since someone might suppose that if He knew of their shortcomings He would be angry with them, He joined to what you have supposed His words: ﴿And indeed Allah﴾, that is, the One whose mercy is all-encompassing and whose greatness is perfect, ﴿is surely All-Knowing﴾, that is, of their intentions and of what they know of what pleases Him and what does not, ﴿Most Forbearing﴾ toward what they fell short of in His obedience, and what they neglected in regard to Him, glorified is He.

When he concluded these verses, in which the permission for the oppressed to fight the oppressors came with the attribute of forbearance, that could suggest that pardoning the rights of people is obligatory, as in the law of Jesus (peace be upon him). So He negated that by His saying, granting permission to those who openly oppose those who expelled them from their homes to expel them from their own homes and make them taste some of the painful punishment that God has threatened them with: ﴿That﴾, that is, the established matter of God's attribute, ﴿and whoever retaliates﴾ among the servants by striking his adversary, ﴿with the like of what he was punished with﴾, that is, treated in the manner of one who seeks a good outcome, ﴿by it﴾, from whatever retaliator it may be, ﴿and then he is wronged﴾, that is, by whatever wrongdoer it may be, ﴿against him﴾, by returning to his dispute in order to take his right.

Since what befalls the one who was wronged, by being overcome, is a return to the start of humiliation and disgrace that is distant from being repaired, He emphasized His promise and said: ﴿God will surely help him﴾, that is, He who has no equal.

Since He restricted that to equivalence, and that is a matter that is hidden and cannot readily be determined, so that transgression may sometimes occur by mistake and one may then assume that help is not given for that reason, God, by His saying, made clear that the accountability applies only to what is intentional. It is also possible that the implication is an encouragement to pardon after the assurance of help: ﴿Indeed God is All-Mighty, All-Wise﴾. And whoever pardons and makes amends has exposed himself to God's pardon for his shortcoming and His forgiveness of his sins. This is an *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are mentioned while each is omitted from the other's place): He mentioned help as an indication of might and wisdom, and He mentioned pardon from Himself, glorified be He, as an indication that pardon from the servant has been omitted. ﴿Indeed God﴾, that is, He who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿is All-Pardoning﴾, that is, toward the one who took retribution from one who wronged him the first time, ﴿All-Forgiving﴾ toward the one who took retribution from one who transgressed against him.

(p-80) When He concluded with these two attributes, He mentioned, as proof of them, a matter that encompasses the benefits and is general to all creatures, in which and through which lies the beneficence of creation and provision. So He said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the recognition that He, glory be to Him, is characterized by these two attributes, ﴿is because Allah﴾, who is characterized by all the attributes of perfection, ﴿causes the night to enter into the day﴾ for the sake of the benefits of the servants, both the evildoer and the doer of good. Thus He erases its darkness with His light. Had He willed to hold people accountable, He would have made it perpetual, and the benefits of the day would have been disrupted. ﴿And causes the day to enter into the night﴾, thus abrogating (yansakh) its light with its darkness. Were it not for this, the benefits of the night would have been disrupted. Or one of them lengthens where it is intended, so that what is naturally disposed to one prevails over the opposite of what the other is naturally disposed to, for the benefits intended by the purpose for which He made that. ﴿And that Allah﴾, by His majesty and greatness, ﴿is All-Hearing﴾ of what can be heard, ﴿All-Seeing﴾, i.e., the one who sees, knows what can be seen, and is continually characterized by that. Therefore He does not need the stillness of the night in order to hear, nor the light of the day in order to see, because He is exempt from accidents (a'rad, attributes that inhere in things). And He, by the completeness of His power and knowledge, does not fear any harm in His pardon, and nothing can escape Him. Or the implied meaning is: that victory and pardon are by virtue of His being All-Powerful and by virtue of His being All-Knowing.

When He described Himself, glorified be He, with attributes that belong to no other, and thereby the insignificance of everything besides Him in His act became clear, He gave the reason in His saying: ﴿That﴾, meaning the attribute of perfect power and all-encompassing knowledge, ﴿is because Allah﴾, who encompasses the attributes of perfection and is able to bring the non-existent into existence and renew what has passed away, including raising the dead and other things, ﴿He alone is the Truth﴾, meaning the Necessarily Existent (wājib al-wujūd), ﴿and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood﴾, meaning calling upon it in worship, while ﴿they do not hear﴾.

Since He, glorified be He, is above everything by His subjugation and sovereignty, He said, belittling them: ﴿besides Him﴾, meaning besides these idols and others. No proof of the falsehood of idols was mentioned here like what He mentioned in Surat Luqman, so the situation called for emphasis with the separating pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl), and He said: ﴿He is the falsehood﴾, because its existence and non-existence are both possible, so it has in its essence nothing but non-existence, like other contingent beings (mumkināt). ﴿And Allah is﴾, because He is the Truth, for whom there is no equal, ﴿He alone is the Most High, the Great﴾, and everything else is lowly and insignificant, under His subjugation and command. Thus He gives life to the dead, as was mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

[p. 82] When the provision that He, glory be to Him, gave to the one who is killed in His path, or who dies otherwise, indicated His giving him life, and He, glory be to Him, indicated this and that He is the best of providers through His greatness, and He concluded with these two attributes, He followed it with another proof of all of that: a witnessed, comprehensive sign that joins the upper and lower worlds and attests to His exaltedness and magnificence. So He said: ﴿Have you not seen﴾, i.e., O addressee, ﴿that Allah﴾, i.e., the One whose power and knowledge encompass all things, ﴿sent down from the sky water﴾, by sending winds that stir up clouds, so that it rains upon the smooth earth.

Since this interrogative (istifham), followed by a negation, carries the sense of affirmation regarding the seeing of the sending down, because it contains the sense of denial, He joined ﴿then the earth becomes﴾ to ﴿sent down﴾ as its consequent, in the customary manner, and He expressed it in the present tense (muḍāriʿ) to alert to the greatness of the blessing, through the long duration of the rain's effect and the continual renewal of its benefit: ﴿then the earth becomes﴾, i.e., after it had been black and dry, dead and lifeless, ﴿green﴾, alive, lush, stirring and growing, with what it contains of the provision of the servants and the cultivation of the lands. He did not put it in the accusative (naṣb) as its answer, lest it imply the negation of greening. This is because the interrogative, insofar as it contains the sense of denial, is a negation of the negation of seeing the sending down, which is the affirmation of seeing the sending down. Thus what is made its answer would be negated, since the answer depends on what it answers. When that on which the dependence rests is negated, the dependent is negated; i.e., when the necessitating cause is negated, the necessitated is negated, and when the cause is negated, the effect is negated, as was previously mentioned in ﴿so that they will have hearts﴾. So if ﴿yuṣbiḥu﴾ (يُصْبِحُ) were put in the accusative as the answer to the interrogative, the meaning would be that the non-greening depends on negating the negation of the sending down, which is the affirmation of the sending down, and this is clearly corrupt. This was conveyed by our shaykh, the Imam Abu al-Fadl, may Allah have mercy on him.

Since this is the production of things from their opposites, because water, in its thinness and fluidity, and earth, in its density and immobility, are each at the furthest remove from plants in their variety, greenness, growth and radiance, He, glory be to Him and exalted, said, alerting to this: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses perfect might and complete knowledge, ﴿is Subtle﴾, i.e., He brings things about from their opposites, ﴿Acquainted﴾, i.e., aware of hidden matters, however fine they may be. So reviving whomever He wills after his death is not far-fetched for Him, nor is His beneficence in provision.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 64:

When that required ending the (divine) disposal (of affairs), because after the mixing of water with earth there must be matters from which vegetation arises, in those strange and varied forms, this made it necessary that He be the absolute Owner. He said: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens﴾, i.e., those from which He sent down the water. And since the context was for establishing the Resurrection, the sole possession of dominion, and the evidence for that, the situation required emphasis by repeating the relative pronoun, so He said: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, i.e., the one in which it is settled. That entails the dominion of the heavens and the earths, for each of them is within the one above it, until the matter reaches His Throne, glory be to Him, which by no means can belong to anyone else.

Since it is familiar to us that an owner is in need of what is in his hand, blamed for withholding it through stinginess and for giving it away through wastefulness, He made clear that He is the opposite of that, saying: ﴿And indeed Allah﴾, i.e., the One who has complete encompassing, ﴿is surely He﴾, i.e., He alone, ﴿the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾, i.e., free of them and of what is in them; He did not create any part of them, or within them, out of need for Himself, but rather for your need, ﴿the Praiseworthy (al-Hamid)﴾ in everything He gives or withholds, because of the hidden and manifest wisdoms in that.

Then he was given further proof of this with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen﴾ — that is, O addressee — ﴿that Allah﴾ — that is, the One possessing the attributes of perfection, of majesty and of beauty — ﴿has subjected to you﴾ out of His bounty ﴿whatever is in the earth﴾, all of it, from its roads and its wide passages, and what is in it of animals and inanimate things, and of crops and fruits. Thus it is known that He is not in need of any of it.

Since the subjection of sailing upon the sea is among the most wondrous of wonders, He said: ﴿and the ship﴾ — that is, He subjected it to you, carrying what you wish of merchandise. Then He explained its subjection by His saying: ﴿running upon the sea﴾ — that is, the surging, turbulent sea with its waves — by a good wind, gently and steadily.

And since the rider in it — despite swift travel and rapid passing — remains as if stationary, as if on the land, the matter of its course is magnified by His saying: ﴿by His command﴾. And since its being held upon the surface of the water, despite its lightness, from sinking is a strange thing, like the holding of the sky over the expanse of the air from falling, He followed it with His saying: ﴿and He holds back the sky﴾, then explained that by His saying in apposition: ﴿from falling﴾ — that is, despite its height, its vastness, and its being without pillars — ﴿upon the earth﴾, which is beneath it.

Since the context requires that it must fall through its dissolution, unless He prevents its falling, because it is a dense, great body whose nature allows nothing but descending, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿except by His permission﴾ — that is, it falls when He permits its falling, at the time He wills to fold up this world and bring into being the world of permanence. And since this supreme generosity and perfect governance is pure munificence without any need at all, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ — that is, the One to whom belong creation and command.

Since all inanimate things are provision for living beings, the context calls for placing before His saying: ﴿with mankind﴾ — that is, despite their wrongdoing — ﴿Most Kind (ra'uf)﴾ — that is, by preserving their inner hearts from deviation through sending the messengers, revealing the books, and establishing the rites, most of which the House that He settled for Ibrahim (peace be upon him) gathers, namely tawhid, prayer, and the Hajj, which leads to the taqwa upon which the surah is built. For mercy (ra'fah), as al-Hiralli said, is the gentlest and most complete of mercy; so the one who is shown ra'fah is upheld by the care of tenderness, until it guards within his inner self, along its course, the manifestation of whatever calls for pardon. Sometimes this guarding is by power, through the setting up of proofs; sometimes it adds to that action the creation of guidance in the heart. This is specific to one who has a kind of connection with the Bestower.

﴿Merciful﴾ — by what is established for them generally of ranks, according to what He has granted them of the fruits (p-86) of that guarding, namely righteous deeds that please Him. This is because, as was mentioned in al-Fatihah, al-Rahim is specially merciful with what the Divine Being is pleased with; and the verification of this point was mentioned earlier in al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 66:

When He, glory be to Him, had explained a number of the foundations of the religion (ummahat al-din), and followed them with assistance for its people against the aggressors, and concluded with what comes after death for the emigrants (muhajirun), as an encouragement to separating from the disbelievers (munabadhat al-kafirin), and had made known what He possesses of perfect knowledge and all-encompassing power, and had illustrated this with various kinds of disposal over the creation of the heavens and the earths, and had pointed out, by way of indication, that all of it is for the benefit of the children of Adam as a blessing from Him, He followed that with what is greater in blessing upon them, saying: ﴿And He is the One who gave you life﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿who gave you life﴾, that is, from inanimateness (al-jamadiyya), after He brought you into existence from non-existence, after you were not anything, as a blessing from Him upon you, independent in itself, which entails the blessing of the benefits of this world already mentioned, so that your life may continue first, and the religious benefits, so that you may profit from remaining (in the afterlife) second. ﴿Then He causes you to die﴾, so that death may be an admonition to those of insight among you, and a restraint for them from the blameworthy character traits to which they have been inclined. ﴿Then He will give you life again﴾, so that He may manifest the decisive judgment and the display of justice in recompense.

When He knew that everything in existence, of substance and of accident, is a blessing upon man, even life and death, and that this was among the most manifest of things, and that his actions turned away from the Lord of these blessings by worshipping other than Him, or by falling short in His right, despite the generality of His bounty and His goodness, He concluded the verse, glory be to Him, with His saying: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾, that is, extremely disbelieving, in that he did not give thanks for these all-encompassing blessings that surround him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 67:

When the mention of the rites (manasik) had preceded, and because of the large number of disbelievers, it may occur to the soul that establishing them is beyond its capacity, God, glorified is He, removed the distress of this question with the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe﴾ [al-Hajj: 38] and what follows it. This produced in us knowledge of His complete disposal through His overwhelming power, and of His all-encompassing knowledge, which requires the turning of the servants toward Him and their all gathering upon Him. Whoever doubts His power to make His religion prevail by defending its people, or disputes this, is an ungrateful disbeliever (kafur). By the manifestation of the first of this address, He reminded them with the last of that address, confirming what He had answered regarding that question, from the perfection of power and the comprehensiveness of knowledge: that He is the One who established for every people the rites through which the order of life is maintained.
