If they agree with the divine command, they are a cause of eternal life, and otherwise they are a cause of perpetual ruin. He, glorified is He, is the One who set for every people the laws that suit them, because by changing the time, by causing the night to enter the day over the passing of days and the succession of months and years, for a reason among the causes, for the sake of testing the servants and bringing forth what He has concealed in the nature of each of them of obedience and disobedience, gratitude and ingratitude, (p-88) an act becomes a benefit by what its causes require after having been a corruption, and the reverse, owing to His power over everything and the manifestation of His power, as He said, may He be exalted, at the first mention of abrogation (naskh, the replacement of one ruling by another):

﴿Do you not know that Allah is competent over all things?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106], and the verses that follow. So He knew that their disputing about it is disbelief. Therefore He followed this, without a conjunction, with His saying, because of the complete connection between them: ﴿For every nation﴾, that is, in every age, ﴿We have appointed﴾, that is, by the greatness that is ours, ﴿a rite (mansak)﴾, that is, a law, for their gathering through it upon their Creator when it agrees with His command, and for their gathering upon their desires when it does not agree with it. It is reported from Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) that the original meaning of mansak in the speech of the Arabs is the place that a person frequents and returns to, whether for good or for evil.

Since what He, glorified is He, willed was bound to occur, He said: ﴿They are performing it﴾, that is, they are worshipping through it, because We defend them against whoever opposes them in it, until its matter is set right for them, for their happiness or their misery through it. So whoever doubts Our power to enable them to perform it is an ungrateful disbeliever. If it agrees with the command, it is profit and faith, and if it opposes it, it is disbelief and loss.

Since He had decreed the manifestation of His religion over all religions, and that the disbelievers, despite their great number, will be overcome after what they are in of arrogance (batar), He informed of that by the expression in the form of a rebuke to them, with His saying, as a consequence of this greatness: ﴿So let them not dispute with you in the matter﴾ (p-89), that is, by what Satan casts to them of doubts so that they may argue with it, such as their attack on your religion through abrogation, by saying: "If it were from Allah, it would not command something today and forbid it tomorrow." For this implies change (bada'), and the matter is not as they claim; rather it indicates knowledge of outcomes and complete power over the enactment of laws, and other doubts besides this, as the allusion to it has passed. So do not turn to them in anything they dispute about, whatever it may be. It is reported that it was revealed because of the argument of the disbelievers, Badil ibn Warqa' and Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Khuza'i and others, about slaughtered animals, and their saying to the believers: "You eat what you have slaughtered, and it is from your killing, but you do not eat what Allah has killed," meaning carrion.

Since the prohibition against disputing with them was in reality a spur and an incitement for him (ﷺ) to turn away from them, because they deserve that, for their scheming is in misguidance, and to turn to his own affair, and since the expression with what has preceded of His turning it toward them was for confirming the command while indicating his honor (ijlal) (ﷺ) from being directly addressed with the prohibition, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And call﴾, that is, make the call (da'wah) to all creation, ﴿to your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has done good to you by sending you, by bringing them to everything He has commanded you with, whenever He commands you. Let their saying not dismay you, for they are certainly defeated, and do not contemplate any outcome of outcomes, but proceed upon the command even if you think that in it is destruction, for there is nothing upon you except that. As for arranging matters on the path of rectitude in manifesting the religion and subduing the obstinate, then refer that to the One who commanded you with those commands, and firmly establish the matter in all of the restraints. Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: ﴿Indeed you﴾, confirming it according to what they hold of denial, ﴿are surely upon a straight guidance﴾, for this is the foundation of the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful, and indeed His paths are change.

When He commanded him to devote himself to what concerned him and to turn away from their disputing with him, He expressed this as a prohibition against their disputing with him. Then He taught him the response if they committed what He had forbidden after he had exerted himself in repelling them, because of their stubbornness and obstinacy. So He said: ﴿And if they dispute with you﴾, that is, about some matter of your religion, with any of the vile statements mentioned earlier or with something else. ﴿Then say﴾, turning away from pointing out the corruption of their religion, which is clearer in its falsehood than anything else: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the King who encompasses might and knowledge, ﴿is most knowing of what you do﴾, threatening them with this, reminding yourself of your Lord's power, and thereby cutting off the dispute from whatever direction it comes, relying on the One who commanded you to this, in the good management of your affairs, in defending you, and in requiting them for what they deserve, according to what He has already known of them. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': Everyone should take this as a model of conduct, for the people of jadal (disputation) have exceeded the bounds of the common folk through their pretentiousness, yet they have not reached the rank of the elite who know things as they really are. The common folk submit to the Shari'ah, the elite know its secrets and realities, and the people of jadal are those in whose hearts there is agitation and unrest.

(p-91) When He had commanded him to turn away from them, and that was hard on the soul, since it longed for victory, He consoled him in that by His saying, beginning a new sentence and substituting it for the object of the conditional clause, as a warning to them: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One for whom there is no equal, ﴿will judge between you﴾, that is, between you, [O Prophet], together with your followers, and them, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, which is the Day of Mutual Loss, ﴿concerning that about which you used to differ﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿differ﴾ concerning the matter of religion, which for you was like an innate disposition. Whoever gives victory on that Day is not concerned with what befell him before it. ﴿And those who wronged will know what [evil] return they will be returned to﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 227]. Al-Baghawi said: "Ikhtilaf (difference) is each of the two opponents going off in a direction opposite to what the other has taken."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 70:

When preserving what occurs among them, in their multitude over long periods of time, was a tremendous matter, He followed it with His saying: ﴿Do you not know that Allah﴾, by the majesty of His might and the greatness of His dominion, ﴿knows what is in﴾. And since the context concerns the preservation of the conditions of the two weighty ones (al-thaqalayn: humankind and the jinn) for judgment between them, and since the most that one might imagine is that some of the jinn could reach eavesdropping (istiraq al-sam') from the lowest heaven, there was no need to mention more than this. So He used the singular, in a form that encompasses the many because it is a genus, and said: ﴿the heaven and the earth﴾, including what occurs among them and among others, from all creatures, animals and otherwise. (p-92)

Since humankind is a place of forgetfulness, unable to retain matters except through a book, He addressed them with what they understand, along with what it contains of wondrous power, and said: ﴿Indeed that﴾, that is, that great matter, ﴿is in a Book﴾, in which everything is written: He decreed its occurrence before it occurred and wrote its recompense. And since gathering all of that into a book is, for humans, something difficult to achieve, He followed it with a clarification of how easy it is for Him, saying: ﴿Indeed that﴾, that is, knowledge of that great matter without a book, and its gathering into a book before its existence and after it, ﴿for Allah﴾, that is, the One whose greatness has no limit, alone, ﴿is easy﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 71:

When He, glorified be He, had informed that doubt would never cease to be a state for them, because of what Satan casts of his insinuations into their hearts, which are receptive to that by virtue of the sickness they have and the corruption within them, until the coming of the Hour; and He followed that with the detailed wisdoms He mentioned and the honoured and excellent rulings, until He concluded by stating that He alone is the Judge over the Hour, instilling awe through the completeness of His knowledge and the all-encompassing scope of His power, He said, marveling at those whom admonition does not benefit and who do not affirm the obligatory, while they affirm the impossible, coordinating it with ﴿and they will not cease﴾ [al-Hajj: 55] ﴿and they worship﴾, meaning in a manner of renewal and continuity, ﴿other than Allah﴾, meaning from the lowest rank among the ranks of Him for whose containing of all attributes of perfection and transcendence above all imperfection all the proofs stand, ﴿for which He has sent down no authority﴾ (p-93), meaning not a single proof of the proofs.

Since it might be supposed that the non-sending down of authority does not negate it, He said, removing this supposition: ﴿and of which they have no knowledge﴾, meaning at all, ﴿and﴾, meaning while the state is that they have none of it. But He made the indication to the attribute for which they deserved destruction, so He said: ﴿for the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who placed worship in other than its proper place by committing this grave and perilous matter. He emphasized the negation and encompassed what is negated by affirming the preposition, so He said: ﴿of helpers﴾, meaning one who would help them against Allah, neither against what they associated with Him nor against anyone else, neither in defending them nor in establishing a proof for their doctrines. Thus He negated that anyone could bring a support that attains the aim, by which the one supported would overcome. As for mere support that does not benefit in the face of the aforementioned insinuations of Satan, that is not negated.

When he had mentioned their acknowledgment of what is known neither by transmission nor by reason, he mentioned their denial of what cannot rightly be denied, saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited﴾, that is, in a continuous and sequential manner, by whoever recites them, ﴿to them﴾, that is, the verses that are heard, with all their greatness and loftiness, ﴿clear﴾, with no obscurity to anyone who has insight into any of what they call to, whether of the roots (al-usul) or the branches (al-furu'). ﴿You recognize﴾ through firasa (perceptive discernment) ﴿in the faces﴾, and this was the original wording, but he replaced the pronoun with an explicit noun that indicates their obstinacy, saying: ﴿in the faces of those who disbelieve﴾, that is, those who are clothed in disbelief, ﴿the denial﴾, that is, the denial which is itself reprehensible, because of the rage (al-ghaydh) that had arisen in them (p-94). Then he explained what appeared in their faces, saying: ﴿They nearly assault﴾, that is, they nearly inflict the assault of violence and brutality, ﴿those who recite to them Our verses﴾, that is, the verses which indicate Our most beautiful names and Our exalted attributes, which establish Our oneness, and which, being clear in the utmost degree as to their being Our speech, contain wisdom and eloquence in which they were unable to match.

When they deserved punishment, because of their denial and their intent to harm the friends of Allah, the consequence was informing them of what they deserved. So he said, signaling anger by turning away from them and commanding the Prophet ﷺ to threaten them: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you﴾, that is, shall I tell you, ﴿of something worse than that?﴾, a great matter of evil that you intended against the servants of Allah who recite His verses to you, and what you suffered of vexation because of that. It is as if it were said, "What is it?" So it was said: ﴿The Fire﴾. Then he resumed his speech, mocking them by mentioning the promise: ﴿Allah has promised it﴾, the Mighty, the Majestic, ﴿to those who disbelieve﴾, as a recompense for them for this intent of theirs. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, ﴿and wretched is the final return.﴾

(p-95) When God, exalted is He, had informed that there is no proof for one who worships other than Him, and threatened those who persist in opposition, He followed this with the point that the proof stands against the fact that this other (than God) is utterly worthless, and has no power to repel what its worshippers are threatened with, nor anything else. How then could it be fit for that exalted rank and that lofty, noble station? So He addressed, calling to those of understanding and alerting them with a general alert: ﴿O mankind﴾.

Since the purpose of a parable is that it be understood, not who uttered it, the verb was made passive in His saying: ﴿a parable has been presented﴾. Its summary: those whom you worship are like you, indeed they are more worthless than you. ﴿So listen carefully﴾, that is, be silent and reflect ﴿to it﴾. Then He explained it with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those you call upon﴾, that is, for your needs, and take as gods, ﴿besides God﴾, that is, besides the King, the Most High, [they are] these idols in which you take pride, and about which you fabricate claims. For denying power to them shows that they are at the lowest of ranks: ﴿they will not create a fly﴾, that is, they have no power to do that now, nor will this attribute ever come to them, at any time or in any state, even though it is small; how then [could they create] what is greater than it? ﴿Even if they gathered together﴾, that is, those whom you claim to be partners, ﴿for it﴾, that is, for creation, they would be like you in this. ﴿And if﴾, that is, and more eloquent than this: they are powerless to resist a fly, for ﴿if the fly should snatch away from them﴾, that is, the fly which was previously said to be beyond their power to create, and which is utterly worthless, ﴿anything﴾ of the things, whether great or small, of what you smear on them of perfume, or place before them of food or other things, ﴿they could not rescue it﴾, that is, they could not recover it, ﴿from it﴾. So in this they are more worthless than you. The point of the comparison with the fly regarding snatching is its audacity (waqaha), and for this reason it is permissible, when conveying the (idea of) repelling, [to use it]. For if its audacity were in the lion, no one would escape it; but wisdom required that the lion's strength be accompanied by aversion, and the fly's audacity by weakness. And it is a singular, not a plural (word). Concerning the combination of al-ʿUbab and al-Muhkam: Ibn ʿUbayda said: "It is the correct form." Then he said: In Kitab ma talhanu fihi al-ʿamma (The Book of What the Common People Mistake) by Abu ʿUthman al-Mazini: "It is said: this is one fly (dhubab), and three flies (adhibba); for both the smallest and largest numbers, it is dhubab. The people's saying dhubaba is an error, so do not say it."

Since this might suggest the fly's strength, He clarified that the intended meaning is other than that, by His saying, as a summary of the whole discourse from its beginning: ﴿the seeker is weak﴾, that is, seeking rescue from the fly, and he is the idols and their worshippers, ﴿and the sought is weak﴾, that is, the fly and the idols; they are alike in weakness, although the idols are weaker by degrees.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 74:

(p-97) When this brought about their ignorance of Allah, he expressed it by His saying: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with the esteem due to Him﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿with the esteem due to Him﴾, in their ascribing to Him, along with His attributes, others, whoever they might be; so how much more so, since they are the most worthless of things. And since it was as if it were said: "What is His esteem?", he said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who combines the attributes of perfection, ﴿is Powerful﴾ over the creation of every possibility, ﴿Mighty﴾, not overcome by anything, while He overcomes everything, unlike their idols and others.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 75:

When the proof had been established that what they call upon besides Him cannot be fit to be a god, any of it, after He had informed that He had not sent down to them any authority for their worshipping of them, and He concluded with what belongs to Him, glorified is He, of the two attributes of power and might, after He had established that dominion belongs wholly to Him, He followed that with His proof, which the vastness of dominion and the strength of authority require, namely the sending down of proofs upon the tongues of the messengers by His commands and prohibitions, which necessitates sincere worship of Him and calls for the punishment of the one who abandons it. So He said: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿chooses﴾, that is, selects and singles out, ﴿from among the angels messengers﴾ for what the sending is fitting for, of punishment and mercy, so none can prevent them from what they were sent for. And there is no doubt that the strength of the messenger derives from the strength of the one who sent him. ﴿And from among mankind﴾ likewise messengers, who convey from Allah what they legislate for His servants, so that through it the proof of transmission is established against them, joined to the authority of reason. Whoever opposes them is a loser, however long his respite may be. And since all of that cannot happen except through knowledge, He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses majesty and beauty (p-98) ﴿is All-Hearing﴾, that is, of whatever can be heard from the Messenger and others, ﴿All-Seeing﴾, that is, a seer, knowing of everything that can be seen and known by reason, unlike their idols.

Since the one described by these attributes may have his attribute limited to some things, He informed that His attributes encompass all things, so He said: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾, that is, the Messengers. [His] knowledge encompasses what they are aware of and what is hidden from them, so they do nothing except by His permission. For He sends a watcher (rasad) before them and behind them, so that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord, even if the ignorant suppose otherwise, because He, glorified and exalted, is veiled behind the causes. It never enters the mind at all that the One whose knowledge encompasses everything and whose power extends to everything would leave one of His Messengers to himself, so that he speaks something He did not send him with, or that He would allow a devil or anyone else to speak upon his tongue. Rather, each of them is preserved in his own self: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ (Q. 53:3), ﴿It is nothing but a revelation revealed﴾ (Q. 53:4), preserved from the distortion of others. ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ (Q. 15:9). ﴿And to Allah﴾, that is, the One who has no equal, alone, ﴿all matters are returned﴾, that is, with the utmost ease, by a decisive promise from which there is no escape, ﴿the matters﴾, on the Day when He manifests Himself for the decisive judgment, so His command will be apparent, with no concealment in it, and nothing among things will issue except in a manner of justice clearly evident to everyone that it comes from Him. No one will have recourse to anyone other than Him. The One who possesses this attribute has the right to legislate whatever He wills, to abrogate from legislation whatever He wills, and to judge as He desires.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 77:

When (Allah, glorified is He) had established that dominion and command belong to Him alone, that He has perfected His law, that He preserves His messengers, and that He grants power to whomever He wills, to any religion He wills, and concluded that with what is suitable for encouragement and warning, and since it was the custom that when a king's commands are made manifest and his callers spread out, those who are inclined to him come forward, He addressed those who come forward to His religion, namely the sincere among people, and said: ﴿O you who believe﴾, meaning, who say "We believe". ﴿Bow down﴾, confirming your saying. ﴿And prostrate yourselves﴾, meaning, pray the prayer that I have legislated for the children of Adam, for it is the foundation of worship, so that it may be a proof of the truthfulness of your affirmation of faith. He specified these two pillars in expressing prayer by them, because they, by contradicting the customary postures, are the ones that indicate humility. Thus expressing prayer by them is very fitting in this surah, which gathers all the groups, among whom are those who find some of the postures indicating humiliation repugnant, because of the arrogance that has overcome them.

When He singled out the most noble of worship, He generalized with His saying: ﴿And worship﴾, meaning, with all kinds of (p-100) worship, ﴿your Lord﴾, the One who bestows upon you every worldly and religious blessing. When He mentioned the generality of worship, He followed it with what may be more general than it, of what has its outward form but may also be without intention, so He said: ﴿And do good﴾, meaning all of it from acts of nearness such as maintaining the ties of kinship, visiting the sick and the like, and of noble character, with intention and without intention, until that becomes a habit for you so that its practice for Allah becomes light upon you. This is close to "Weep, and if you cannot weep, then feign weeping." Abu Hayyan said: He began with the specific and then with the more general.

﴿So that you may prosper﴾, meaning, so that your state may be that of one who hopes for success, which is attaining the sought-after object. Ibn al-Qattaa said: aflaha al-rajul (the man prospered): he attained the bliss of the Hereafter, and falaha is also a dialect form of it. In the combination of al-Ubab and al-Muhkam: al-falh and al-falah: success and endurance. In the revelation: ﴿Certainly the believers have prospered﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1], meaning they attained lasting endurance. In a report: aflaha al-rajul: he gained victory. And whoever attains good is called muflih (successful).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 22, verse 78:

Since jihad (striving in the way of God) is the foundation of worship, and although it is literally applied to fighting the disbelievers, it is also suitable to encompass every enjoining of good and forbidding of evil, with wealth, with the self, with speech, with action, with the sword and other means, and every exertion in refining the self and sincering one's deeds, He concluded with it, saying: ﴿And strive for God with the striving due to Him﴾, that is, the Sovereign, the Greatest, who has no equal in everything that is ascribed to Him, glory be to Him, from Whom nothing escapes, just as nothing escapes from the contained (maẓrūf) from its container (ẓarf). ﴿With the striving due to Him﴾ means by exhausting one's capacity in carrying out everything He has commanded of striving against the enemy and the self, in the manner He has commanded, through the Hajj, the raid, and other things, a striving that befits what the attribution to His pronoun, glory be to Him, conveys of sincerity and strength. For indeed, all who would turn you away from any part of it will be destroyed.

When He, glory be to Him, had commanded these commands, He followed them with some of what is due in gratitude to Him, and it is like the explanation of what came before it, so He said: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, that is, He chose you to place the message among you and the Messenger from among you, and made him the most noble of the messengers, his religion the most honourable of religions, his Book the greatest of books, and made you, by virtue of being his followers, the best of nations. ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion﴾ which He has chosen for you ﴿any hardship﴾, that is, any constraint by which there would be some kind of excuse for one who falls short in the lesser and greater striving, just as He placed it upon those before you, as some of it was mentioned earlier in al-Baqarah and elsewhere, namely ﴿the religion of﴾

Since the first addressed by this were the Quraysh, then Mudar, and all of them were, in literal truth, sons of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿your father Ibrahim﴾, that is, the one who abandoned the worship of idols and forbade it, and affirmed the oneness of God and commanded His monotheism. O you who are bound by imitating the fathers! Then adhere to his religion because he is a father, and because I have commanded it. He is a father in literal truth to some of the addressed people of the community, and in figurative truth to others, through honour and reverence, so the address encompasses all. For this reason He urged them to his religion by the explanation in His saying: ﴿He﴾, that is, Ibrahim, peace be upon him, ﴿named you the Muslims﴾ in earlier times ﴿before﴾, that is, before the sending down of this Qur'an. Thus He honoured your mention and praised you in former ages and ancient times, so He recorded his praise in the books of the prophets, recited to the rabbis and monks, and He also named you Muslims. ﴿And in this﴾ Book which was sent down to you after the sending down of those books, just as I informed you of his supplication in His saying: ﴿and from our offspring a Muslim community submissive to You﴾ [al-Baqarah: 128], because by the absence of hardship the name corresponds to the named. It is also permissible, and perhaps it is better, that ﴿He named you﴾ be an explanation of the command to the due striving after its explanation in His saying: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, so the pronoun refers to God, the Exalted. The goodness of this is supported by the reading of Ubayy, may God be pleased with him, which uses the divine name (al-Jalalah) in place of the pronoun, meaning that every nation named itself by a name of its own accord, while God, the Exalted, specified you with the name Islam, derived for Him from His name "al-Salam" (the Peace), together with what He specified you with of the name of faith (iman), derived for Him from His name al-Mu'min (the Granter of Security), so He established this name for you in His Books, and chose you to follow His Messenger.

Since the name, when it originates from God, the Exalted, whether through one of His prophets or without an intermediary, is informative about the essence of the named, and the sense was: He removed hardship from you and named you with Islam so that you would be the most submissive of nations, so that you would be the best of them, He gave the reason for this meaning by His saying: ﴿that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿because he is your best, and the witness is best﴾. And since the context is for establishing the absolute description of Islam only, the situation did not require fronting the adverbial phrase, unlike the verse of al-Baqarah, as that is for establishing what is more specific than this. ﴿And that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾ by what is in your natures of goodness, that their messengers conveyed to them the messages of their Lord, because you have honoured the messengers their due honour, and did not differentiate between any of them, and you know their reports from your Book upon the tongue of your Messenger, may blessings and peace be upon him. By all of that you became the best of them, so you were qualified for testimony, and your testimony was valid, and the just judge (al-Hakam al-'Adl) was with you. This indicates that the testimony of one who is not Muslim is not accepted.

Since He urged them to be the best of people, this resulted in His saying: ﴿So establish﴾, that is, as a consequence of My bestowing these blessings upon you and My elevating you to this noble station, I say to you: establish ﴿the prayer﴾, which is the purification of your hearts and the connection between you and your Lord, ﴿and give zakat﴾, which is the purification of your bodies and the connection between you and your brethren, ﴿and hold fast to God﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, in all that He has commanded you, of the rites mentioned earlier and others, so that you may be pious, and He will defend you against whoever wants to come between you and any of them, and will protect you from the terror of the Hour. Then He gave the reason for His being fit to be held fast to by them by His saying: (He) that is, He alone, ﴿is your Protector﴾, that is, the one who manages all your affairs, so He will help you against everyone who opposes you, to the extent that you will be able to manifest this religion through the rites of the Hajj and others. Then He gave the reason for the command to hold fast and for His singular guardianship by His saying: ﴿So excellent is the Protector, and excellent is the Helper﴾, that is, He is. For when He takes charge of someone, He suffices him for everything that concerns him, and when He helps someone, He raises him above everyone who contends with him. "My servant does not cease to draw near to Me with voluntary acts until I love him; so when I love him..." (the hadith), "Indeed, he whom You befriend is not humiliated, and he whom You oppose is not honoured." This is the fruit of piety, and what came before it of acts of obedience is its evidence. Thus the end of the surah has been joined to its beginning, and its conclusion has been returned to its opening. God knows best His intent and the secrets of His Book, and He is the Guide to what is right.
